answer.why: As an insider, 'Confirmed & Substantive' made me laugh straight away, because it is exactly the wording on a letter after probation or promotion and only someone who has lived it would use it. It signals the game knows the service's small details. 'Minister Salary' is the obvious, slightly clickbait name that everyone in Singapore has an opinion on, so it feels like it would be a joke or a rant rather than a careful sim. I would still be a bit wary that outsiders wouldn't get the first name, but I am the target player.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A cheeky, headline-grabbing game about climbing to the top for the pay, probably heavy on the million-dollar benchmark controversy, with a satirical or cynical edge and perhaps a lot of money numbers. I would worry it gets the details wrong and plays to outsider stereotypes about civil servants chasing a salary, and I would half expect a cheap political jab.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A drier, more authentic workplace sim about the real texture of a public service career: probation, appraisals, promotions to substantive appointments, and the quiet bureaucratic jargon insiders recognise. It would feel understated and knowing, with humour in the wording of appraisals and meetings, more about surviving and moving through the system than about the top pay.

worst_moment.what: Running in the GRC and losing at 48.2%, with the AO, the folder and the CEP never coming back. The run ended just as the setups were due to pay off.

answer.held_back_by: Mostly the REP stat. I stayed at 51 while INTEG and COMP were maxed, so I was clean and competent but not known. In the end the ward result was about the team and the party, not me, as the card said. The game seems to reward visibility over integrity.
answer.ending_fair_why: It is plausible that a civil servant parachuted into a GRC could lose 48.2% with low name recognition, and the card owned that. But I wanted to see the AO and the folder resolved, so it felt abrupt.
answer.chase_next: I would chase the Minister ending: build REP early through visible postings and keep my integrity, to see if the politics path and the pay actually connect. I also want to know which salary figure is real.
answer.play_again_why: I want to see what REP does and whether the dangling threads ever pay off, though I would not start right now.

tone_breaks.note: The two figures conflict and the game never explains which is real. A Deputy Secretary's package would not look like either, and it undercuts the benchmarking premise.
I'd expect a current grade name here, since Superscale is dated. Senior Director at Superscale also sounded off to me, and I noticed because it's my world.

answer.title_fit_why: The game was about being confirmed in a post and the slow, quiet accumulation of standing, not about the pay. The salary header was the least convincing part.
